attrs.evidence: probe_execlaunch_v09_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against verbatim frozen v0.8.0 copies — P-3, where a genuine JS artifact declaration plus an unrelated spawn() yields implementation_provenance 'observed' for impl-c-derive-v0.8.0 against the real JS closure digest; and P-3F, which RUNS the film-plane version against the real ic32_film binary's genuine digest and a run() that returns a film produced earlier, so no C process executes during the observation and film_provenance is still 'observed'. P-3F is the cleanest statement of the separation this project has been building: the film IS semantically valid, replaySemFilm proves it, and the claimed execution provenance is false. 5/5 confined live: no launcher parameter on either path, a catalog entry that carries no action and whose entrypoint must lie inside its own hashed closure, an invocation refused as non-canonical when it carries a function, a catalog that cannot be edited after construction, and sessions reported as a list. derive_realm_battery.mjs 20/20, derive_battery.mjs 45/45, bridge/film_check.mjs 14/14.
attrs.statement: ARTIFACT OBSERVATION DOES NOT ESTABLISH EXECUTION PROVENANCE UNLESS THE MECHANISM INVOKED IS MECHANICALLY DERIVED FROM THE ARTIFACT OBSERVED. Equivalently, and this is the operative form: a launch descriptor may not carry both the evidence and an independent executable action. @1 let the caller pick the label, @2 let it pick the name a registration would report, @3 made the authority hash real bytes and then call a function the caller had supplied beside them. Each revision closed one supplier and left the next; the pattern is that any field a caller controls on the launch path becomes the provenance. So the caller supplies NOTHING on that path. ObservedExecutionHost is constructed with an IMMUTABLE EXECUTOR CATALOG — family name to {kind, entrypoint, artifact_closure}, deep-frozen, injective, refusing an entrypoint outside its own hashed closure and refusing any entry field beyond those three. The transport for each kind is written in the host. execute(registry, req) names a family and nothing else; the invocation is DATA and is canonicalised, which refuses a function outright. Both authorities — derivation and film — share this host and share no semantics with it: it cannot re-derive a result, replay a film, or say what either means. Duplicating the semantic boundary is the fence; duplicating the mechanism reproduced the defect in both planes, which is how it was found twice. Acceptance reports executor_sessionS, plural. The key is over BYTES, so two launches producing byte-identical output share it; reporting a single session id claims a uniqueness the key cannot support, and @3's implementation overwrote the earlier record besides. DECLARED OPEN, unchanged: hash-then-launch supports 'the host observed artifact X immediately before requesting execution of path P'. It is NOT a proof that the OS executed those exact bytes under every filesystem race, and it is not hardware-attested executable identity. The node binary, its flags and the standard library are uncovered for a JS entry; every shared object the loader binds is uncovered for a native one.
